newsitem.title: GERMANY: German flour millers see steady flour consumption.
newsitem.headline: German flour millers see steady flour consumption.

text.p: The association of German flour millers ADH expected little changes in soft wheat and rye processing in the 1996/97 (July/June) season after 6.92 million tonnes were handled nationally in 1995/96, an official said.
"Domestic flour consumption looks set to be steady but flour exports are hard to gauge at this stage...they vary between six and 12 percent of total volumes," he said by telephone from Bonn.
Some 8.4 percent of the total 95/96 wheat and rye flour output was exported and exports in the first half of the new season had "not been bad," he said.
ADH represents between two thirds and three quarters of German milling capacity.
Traditional markets for German flour are countries around the Mediterranean, Africa and the former Soviet Union.
Within the 95/96 figure for processed grain volumes, wheat accounted for 85 percent at 5.88 million tonnes, Bonn farm ministry figures showed.
Using a flour extraction rate of 79.3 percent, this translated into 4.66 million tonnes of wheat flour output.
Germany's 96/97 wheat crop of 18.94 million tonnes was up 6.6 percent form 95/96 but rye, at 4.17 million, was off 7.8 percent, according to offical data.
The ADH official said millers were unhappy with reports of downward pressure on domestic grain prices as they did not reflect consumers' high buying-in levels.
"We haven't felt any price weakness, British feed wheat may be bought by feed mixers for 265 marks cif but that does not at all reflect the bread wheat market," he said.
"We are seeking premium qualities with 14 percent protein and sellers resist anywhere below 295-300 marks."
This put domestic premium wheat at par with fob Baltic export prices.
